newsitem.title: INDONESIA: PRESS DIGEST - Indonesian newspapers - Sept 24.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indonesian newspapers - Sept 24.

text.p: Following is a summary of major Indonesian political and business stories in leading newspapers, prepared by Reuters in Jakarta. Reuters has not checked the stories and does not guarantee their accuracy. Telephone: (6221) 384-6364. Fax: (6221) 344-8404.
More than 175,000 Indonesians die of tuberculosis every year making it the second most common cause of death.

Education Minister Wardiman Djojonegoro admitted that two paintings, recently offered for auction by Christies in Singapore, had been stolen from the National Musuem in Jakarta and the theft could have been an inside job.

A lawsuit brought by two daughters of founding president Sukarno against the armed forces chief of sociopolitical affairs, Lieutenant-General Syarwan Hamid, was settled by mediation. The general had been quoted as saying Megawati Sukarnoputri and her sister Sukmawati were planning a "people's power" rebellion.

The armed forces have reshuffled 100 senior officiers in all four services, with one-time rising star Major-General Hendropriyono recalled to headquarters pending an assignment in the civilian administration.
State-owned Bank BNI is ready to sell more than 1 billion shares to the public at a nomial price of 500 rupiah, officials said in releasing details of the bank's public offer.
Tourism department figures show that 11 star-rated hotel projects in Jakarta worth around 500 billion rupiah have been delayed due to financing problems.
